manuals.title: Academic Agents
manuals.description: How to use AIH Academic Agents for specialized educational and research workflows.
manuals.content:
Academic Agents are specialized academic assistants invoked from within a conversation for particular learning, teaching, research, or scholarly tasks. Your Primary Experience remains the persistent way AI Scholar Hub works with you.

To use an Academic Agent:
1. Keep or choose the appropriate Primary Experience in the header.
2. Open Agents from the composer.
3. Choose the specialized Agent that best matches the task, such as Literature Review, Research Gap Finder, Evidence of Learning / Oral Defense, Debate & Sparring Partner, or Research Integrity & Contribution Reviewer.
4. Describe the task clearly.
5. Supply permitted documents or select authorized Knowledge Sources when useful.
6. Review the result critically and follow academic-integrity requirements.

Academic Agents do not override your role, institution, Knowledge Source permissions, or security controls. An Agent can use only the capabilities and Knowledge Sources authorized for your account.

manuals.title: Account and Login Help
manuals.description: Sign-in, account access, password, and institution-login guidance.
manuals.content:
Your AI Scholar Hub account is associated with an institution and role.

If you cannot sign in:
1. Confirm that you are using the approved sign-in method for your institution.
2. Check that you are using the correct account or institutional email.
3. If local passwords are enabled, use the approved password-reset process.
4. If your institution requires SSO, use the configured Google or Microsoft sign-in method.
5. Contact your Institution Admin if your account is disabled, missing, or assigned to the wrong institution.

Never provide passwords, authentication tokens, API keys, or recovery codes to AIH Support.

manuals.title: Common Errors
manuals.description: Meaning and recommended action for common user-facing AIH errors.
manuals.content:
Common AI Scholar Hub errors usually fall into these categories:

Authentication required:
Your session may have expired. Sign in again.

Permission denied or unauthorized:
Your role, institution, group membership, or capability does not permit the requested operation. Contact the appropriate administrator if you believe your access is incorrect.

Document unavailable:
The document may not be in your authorized Knowledge Source scope or may still be processing.

Upload rejected:
The file may be unsupported, unsafe, malformed, or contain active content that AIH does not accept.

Agent unavailable:
The Academic Agent may not be enabled for your role or institution.

Temporary service error:
Retry after a short interval. If the error persists, report the visible error and the operation you were performing.

Do not work around access-control or document-security errors by attempting alternate unauthorized paths.

manuals.title: Getting Started with AI Scholar Hub
manuals.description: How to begin using AI Scholar Hub and choose the right learning or research experience.
manuals.content:
AI Scholar Hub provides role-aware AI assistance for learning, teaching, research, and institutional knowledge.

Getting started:
1. Sign in with your approved AIH account.
2. Choose the Primary Experience appropriate to your continuing work.
3. Use normal chat for general assistance.
4. Invoke Academic Agents from the composer when a particular task needs specialized educational, research, or scholarly help.
5. Use authorized Knowledge Sources when your institution has provided documents or information for your class, group, or institution.
6. Use Skills when a compact reusable workflow is helpful.
7. Review AI-generated answers critically and follow academic-integrity requirements.

Available functions depend on your role, institution, group membership, and permissions.

manuals.title: Knowledge Sources and Documents
manuals.description: How institutional, course, group, and personal Knowledge Sources are used safely in AIH.
manuals.content:
Knowledge Sources allow AI Scholar Hub to answer using documents and information you are authorized to access.

AIH may provide:
- institution-wide Knowledge Sources;
- department, course, class, or group Knowledge Sources;
- instructor-authorized materials;
- your own permitted personal files.

Access is hierarchical and permission-controlled. A document being stored in AIH does not automatically make it available to every user.

When using Knowledge Sources:
1. Select or upload only material you are authorized to use.
2. Ask questions that relate to the available material.
3. Check important answers against the original sources.
4. Do not upload secrets, credentials, or material you are not authorized to share.

If expected course or institutional material is unavailable, contact the instructor or Institution Admin responsible for that Knowledge Source.

manuals.title: Using AI Scholar Hub — User Guide
manuals.description: Practical guide for students and regular users: chat, learning experiences, Knowledge Sources, documents, Academic Agents, permissions, and help.
manuals.content:
AI Scholar Hub helps you learn, ask questions, work with authorized knowledge, and use educational AI assistance provided by your institution.

What you can use
The features visible to you depend on your role, institution, group membership, and permissions. You may have access to:
- a Primary Experience such as the Undergraduate Socratic Tutor;
- Academic Agents approved for your institution;
- Tools such as web search or code where permitted;
- compact Skills;
- personal documents you are permitted to upload;
- course, group, or institution Knowledge Sources.

Starting a conversation
1. Sign in with your approved AI Scholar Hub account.
2. Choose the Primary Experience appropriate to your continuing work from the header.
3. Enter your question in normal language.
4. Invoke an Academic Agent from the composer when the current task needs specialized help.
5. Use Tools, Skills, or Knowledge Sources when useful and permitted.
6. Continue with follow-up questions when you need clarification or deeper explanation.

Primary Experience
Your Primary Experience is the persistent way AI Scholar Hub works with you. Examples include the Undergraduate Socratic Tutor, Instructor Assistant, and Research Synthesizer.

Academic Agents
Academic Agents provide specialized assistance for particular educational, research, or scholarly tasks. Invoke Agents from the composer. They do not replace your underlying Primary Experience.

Tools
Tools provide operational capabilities such as web search, code execution, Skills, memory, connected resources, or structured-output creation where available.

Skills
Release I includes two curated reusable workflows:
- Study a Topic — focused explanation, examples, checks for understanding, and recap.
- Analyze a Research Paper — research question, methods, findings, limitations, and key claims.

Knowledge Sources
Knowledge Sources allow AI Scholar Hub to use documents and information you are authorized to access, including institutional, course, class, group, instructor-provided, or personal material.

A document being stored in AI Scholar Hub does not automatically make it available to every user. Access remains controlled by institution, group, course, and user permissions.

Research Integrity & Contribution Reviewer
This Academic Agent provides professor-style review of accuracy, evidence, methodology, novelty and contribution, citation integrity, reasoning, overclaiming, and revision priorities. It can verify only material it can actually inspect and should not declare research misconduct without adequate evidence.

Academic integrity
AI Scholar Hub is designed to strengthen learning, authorship, evidence, attribution, and scholarly judgment. AIH should distinguish evidence from inference and uncertainty, preserve provenance, and never fabricate citations, evidence, measurements, or source access.

If something is missing
If you cannot see an expected Agent, Tool, Skill, Knowledge Source, course document, or other capability, do not attempt to bypass the restriction. Access may depend on your role, institution, group, or course membership.

Students and regular users should normally contact their instructor or Institution Admin when expected access is missing.

Getting help
Use AIH Support for questions about Primary Experiences, Academic Agents, Tools, Skills, Knowledge Sources, documents, account access, workflows, and common errors.

For unresolved problems, provide the visible error message and describe what you were trying to do. Never provide passwords, tokens, API keys, or other secrets to Support.
